1.

Sri Brijesh Pratap Singh, learned Aga for the State apprised the Court that he has received
instructions in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be
disposed of on merit.

2. Heard Sri Ramesh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Yogesh Kumar Mishra,
learned counsel for the informant and Sri Brijesh Pratap Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 687 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 506 IPC, Police Station Sihani Gate, District Ghaziabad, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted, on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter and prima facie, it appears to be a case of civil dispute and only Narendra Kuamr vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: allegation against the applicant is that he did not execute sale deed in favour of the informant in spite of receiving consideration for the same from him.

5. He further submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and it is the fault of the informant due to which, till date, sale deed could not be executed and even it appears that as per allegation, applicant breached the contract and, therefore, no criminal liability can be fastened against him.

6. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and all the offences are punishable with maximum punishment of seven years but in spite of that local police is trying to arrest the applicant.

7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submitted that by playing fraud, applicant received huge amount of money from the informant and thereafter did not execute sale deed in his favour but both the counsels could not dispute the fact that from the FIR, it reflects that it is a case of breach of contract.
8. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Considering the fact that present dispute appears to be dispute of civil nature and all the offences are punishable with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is not having any criminal history, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
